name: Queen's University Belfast

settingEvidence.evidence: A CAMPUS UNIVERSITY AT THE HEART OF BELFAST CITY

fees.text: £9,790 per year for full-time undergraduates who normally live in England, Scotland or Wales (the 2026/27 fee; students who normally live in Northern Ireland pay £4,985). The 2027/28 fee is not published yet; Queen's says the fees will be updated when the new fees are known.

source.evidence: Students who normally live in England, Scotland and Wales (GB Students), will be charged tuition fees of £9,790 per annum for full time undergraduate programmes.

livingCosts.text: Queen's halls cost about £119–£243 a week with all bills included (2026/27). Undergraduates can choose a 40 or 48 week contract.

source.evidence: our comprehensive, all-inclusive accommodation prices vary from £119 up to £243 per week

events.label: Queen's Business School undergraduate information evening, 6pm to 9pm (not a full open day)

openDays.text: Queen's holds undergraduate open days every June and October (the last was Saturday 3 October 2026; June 2027 dates are not announced yet). Queen's Business School has an in-person undergraduate information evening on Wednesday 25 November 2026, 6pm to 9pm, at its Student Hub (185 Stranmillis Road). Campus tours run on Mondays and Fridays.

source.evidence: Business School Undergraduate Information Evening - Wed, 25 Nov 2026 18:00:00 GMT

contextual.summary: Queen's does not publish contextual-offer criteria on the web pages we could read. Its widening-access route is the Pathway Opportunity Programme (up to two A-level grades off the offer), which is only open to students who live and study in Northern Ireland.

source.evidence: Receive a potential reduction of up to two A-level grades in your offer, which will be dependent on your performance in the programme and the course you apply for.

programmes.name: Pathway Opportunity Programme (Business pathway)
programmes.summary: Widening-access programme for Northern Ireland students in the first year of A-levels (or similar), with online study, events and a one-week summer school on campus; the Business pathway covers Business Management, Accounting, Finance and Economics.
programmes.whoCanApply: Students aged 16-19 who normally live in Northern Ireland and study full-time at a school or college in Northern Ireland, in year 1 of a two-year Level 3 course (e.g. A-levels), where neither parent has a university degree, with at least five GCSEs at grade C/4 or above including English Language, and who meet at least one of: free school meals or EMA, carer, NISRA area of disadvantage postcode, newcomer pupil, refugee or asylum seeker, care experienced, or substantial experience of social workers or statutory support services. Open only to students who live and study in Northern Ireland.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Section A (all required): ordinarily resident in Northern Ireland; in full-time education at a school or college in Northern Ireland; in year 1 of a two-year Level 3 qualification (e.g. A-levels); neither parent has attended university or has an undergraduate degree; at least five Level 2/GCSE passes at grade C/4 or above including GCSE English Language; meet any GCSE subject requirements and study the right Level 3 subjects for the chosen pathway; aspire to study at Queen's University Belfast. Section B (at least one): free school meals or EMA within the last 2 years; carer for a family member or dependant; live in a NISRA 'area of disadvantage' postcode; 'newcomer' pupil; refugee or asylum seeker; care experienced (automatically offered a place if Section A is met); substantial experience of a social worker or other statutory support services. The programme is open to students aged 16-19.
benefits: Guaranteed conditional offer or guaranteed interview on a course within your Pathway subject
Possible reduction of up to two A-level grades in your offer, depending on your performance in the programme and the course you apply for
£1000 Kilwaughter Foundation bursary awarded in your first semester at Queen's
One-week summer school staying in Queen's student accommodation (Elms Village), with lectures and a final assessed piece of work
programmes.offerReduction: Up to two A-level grades, depending on performance in the programme and the course applied for
programmes.subjects: Business pathway: Business Management, Accounting, Finance and Economics (13 subject pathways in total)
programmes.yearGroup: Year 13 in Northern Ireland (the first year of a two-year Level 3 course such as A-levels, which is Year 12 in England)

runs.text: Programme events run January to December 2027; the Business pathway attends Summer School 2: Monday 28 June to Friday 2 July 2027

programmes.infoNote: 2027 programme. Applications opened on 29 September 2026 and close at noon on 4 November 2026. Summer school dates are from the programme's Key Dates page. Only open to students who live and study in Northern Ireland.

source.evidence: They will close noon, November 4 2026.
